subject: trapdoor spider
title: This Spider's Rear End Is a Hard Disc That Seals Its Burrow Shut

scenes.text: This spider's back end looks like an ancient coin. It's actually a door.
Cyclocosmia trapdoor spiders have an abdomen that ends flat, hardened into a thick disc.
It's only about one to one and a half centimeters across, ridged like a carved seal.
When danger comes, the spider dives head first down its burrow.
The disc wedges tight against the walls and becomes a false bottom. Scientists think it blocks hunters like spider wasps.
Whatever digs in finds no spider. Just a wall, and the wall is its back.

description:
Cyclocosmia trapdoor spiders, found in the southeastern United States, Mexico and Southeast Asia, have an abruptly truncated abdomen ending in a hardened, ribbed disc about 1 to 1.5 cm across.
When threatened, the spider dives head first into its burrow and the disc plugs the shaft like a false bottom (phragmosis), thought to keep out predators such as parasitic spider wasps.
What would you call this spider?
thumbnail_text: ITS BACK END IS A DOOR
first_comment: Each species has a different number of ribs on its disc, so scientists can identify it from its rear. Coin, seal or manhole cover?
